framework_name: The Load-Budget-Binding Ledger: a pre-rollout causal account of transform-replay data generation (load vector from the transform spec x budget vector from the source demo -> survival law -> survivor coverage and imitability -> binding-constraint policy map)
core_claim: Every attempt a MimicGen-style generator makes is a typed LOAD vector applied to a demonstration's BUDGET vector, and both are computable in closed form from the source hdf5, the transform specification, and the task geometry alone -- before a single simulator step. The load side (diversity causes) decomposes per object and per channel: frame shifts of the grasped vs receiving object, symmetry-weighted lever-amplified rotation, junction/bridge length in relative inter-object displacement, absolute workspace geography, and scene clearance; the budget side (quality causes) is the demo's slack profile: speed headroom against the 0.05 m per-step action clip, residual contact-funnel margin, and -- on the imitability axis -- strategy consistency across sources and non-demonstrated-motion share. Generation outcomes (DGR decline, source skew and extinction, receiving-object kill asymmetry, rotation surcharge) are first-passage events of load exceeding budget at the tightest funnel, while policy outcomes are governed one level up by which of four pre-computable resources is BINDING for the task -- survivor coverage at tolerance-scaled radius, supervision consistency, strategy multiplicity, or survivor margin -- which is why most data-composition interventions were null (they moved slack cells) and why DGR is structurally an imperfect proxy (it integrates the survival law but is blind to survivor imitability and marginal-survivor mass). The framework's two structural anchors are theorems about the generator's own code path, not fits: (i) pure translation of a reference object leaves the within-segment action sequence bit-identical to the source, so all translation-induced failure enters through exactly four leaks (junction, arm reconfiguration, snapshot staleness, noise); (ii) the interpolation bridge is hard-coded to 5 steps against a 0.05 m clip, giving a 0.25 m transit ceiling and threshold-shaped, not linear, failure in junction length.

explains:
[
  {"observation": "O1: DGR falls with transform magnitude in 9/9 tasks", "explanation_via": "Every load channel is monotone in region widening: junction load L_j and lag Λ (fixed-step bridge), per-object channel vector m1/m2 with lever-amplified rotation, absolute workspace excursion, staleness exposure -- spent against fixed demo budgets (headroom, funnel margin). The bridge's 0.25 m transit ceiling predicts a threshold-shaped, not linear, decline -- a sharper form than the observation itself. Factors: interpolation bridge, channel load vector, workspace geography, headroom, funnel budget."},
  {"observation": "O2: survivors skew to few sources; some go extinct (mug s7 0/56, square s2 0/160 even in nearest bins)", "explanation_via": "Per-source success is a product of per-subtask survival factors of source-specific moduli -> heavy-tailed across sources; extinction = budget below noise floor already at zero displacement, i.e. source-intrinsic, matching the harm-hunt. Budget respecified as tempo/headroom per the empirical screen (geometric candidates were null). Factors: lag-absorption headroom, contact-funnel residual budget."},
  {"observation": "O3: at matched scene distance the filter preferentially kills receiving-object-displaced attempts (6/8 tasks; failures concentrate late, 0.78-1.00 of fails)", "explanation_via": "Three converging mechanisms, with an identification argument: (i) gripper-closure contraction resets pick-side error while receiver displacement injects error downstream of the last funnel and upstream of the tightest tolerance (C_place << C_grasp); (ii) staleness loads on the receiver (insertions push it); (iii) the bridge channel is provably SYMMETRIC in pick vs receiver, so it cannot be the cause -- isolating (i)+(ii). The same C_s table predicts the 2/8 sign-flips (mug/hammer: tight funnel at grasp, early failures). Factors: channel load vector, funnel capacity C_s, pose staleness, interpolation bridge (as exclusion)."},
  {"observation": "O4: source quality moves policy +7~22pp causally at matched distance (5/5 tasks)", "explanation_via": "Source swap at frozen distance moves only the quality cells: survivor margin (headroom/budget -> μ) and supervision consistency/proficiency inheritance (generated demos are stylistic clones, so the pool's demonstrator population IS the source set). Factors: headroom, marginal-survivor mass μ, strategy consistency H(A|S)."},
  {"observation": "O5: DGR is an imperfect proxy -- one high-DGR source is toxic for learning; noise ablation DGR +33pp / policy -30~40pp", "explanation_via": "DGR integrates only the survival law; it is blind to two survivor-quality channels. Noise half: removing ε lets zero-margin trajectories survive while destroying the robustness probe (μ). Toxic-source half: a strategy-outlier source injects contradictory supervision at shared states -- cross-source inconsistency DGR cannot see; also a high-slack demo (long dwells, huge run-up) maximizes survival while teaching stalling. Arbitration rule: within-source anomalies -> μ; cross-source -> H(A|S). Factors: action noise/ε, marginal-survivor mass μ, strategy consistency."},
  {"observation": "O6: policy cliffs in all-sources-far corners (machine-only-far -24.1pp)", "explanation_via": "Joint per-object survivor coverage: corners have near-zero mass in the per-object JOINT sense even when scalar-distance coverage looks fine, because the filter thins attempts precisely along the receiving-object and corner channels where budgets are tightest (links O3 to O6); the kinematic/geography channel is corner-shaped, not radial. Factors: success-filter projector, workspace geography, channel load vector."},
  {"observation": "O7: coverage need is task-dependent (coffee far-removal -9.7pp with far-bin-concentrated gap; stack unharmed)", "explanation_via": "Coverage kernel radius is tolerance-scaled, ρ = α C_s: coffee's mm-scale pod-slot clearance gives a tight kernel so far removal binds; stack's wide yaw-free footprint leaves coverage slack at 40% removal. Factors: funnel capacity C_s, success-filter projector."},
  {"observation": "O8: rotation adds difficulty beyond position (coffee mirror -27.9pp below distance-only extrapolation; threading position-flip on-trend)", "explanation_via": "Rotation breaks the translation-invariance lemma via three additive penalties translation provably lacks: lever-arm hidden excursion 2r sin(Δψ/2) uncounted by d_pos, wrist-joint demand with silent persistent saturation, and yaw-tolerance anisotropy keyed to interface symmetry (cube/needle null, machine/hammer/mug near-deterministic -- confirmed per-object in e1). Threading's flip loads only position channels -> on-trend; coffee's mirror is the Δψ≈π limit of all three. Additive (not super-additive) composition per the measured null interaction. Factors: translation-invariance lemma, channel load vector, workspace geography (wrist), funnel capacity."},
  {"observation": "S1: transform_uniform density redistribution null (pooled p=0.766 at real dosage)", "explanation_via": "Binding-constraint logic: density redistribution inside already-covered support is a slack-cell intervention -- coverage was saturated at these capacities, so it cannot bind. The framework predicts nulls as nulls. Factors: success-filter projector (survivor coverage), funnel capacity C_s."},
  {"observation": "S2: ancestry balancing harms stack only (-7.5pp, 6/6 seeds; distance distribution identical to baseline)", "explanation_via": "Balancing reinjects the incompatible minority strategy cluster's mass, raising H(A|S) at shared states while distance is untouched -- exactly what was measured; task selectivity = inter-cluster incompatibility gap G, computable from source demos alone (stack top). Survival-margin logic alone would wrongly predict universal harm -- the binding-cell layer is what recovers selectivity. Factor: strategy multiplicity/consistency."},
  {"observation": "S3: density-direction split (square near-heavy +6.7pp; coffee/threading far-heavy; stack null)", "explanation_via": "Sign rule: near-heavy helps iff near-goal-shell supervision divergence exceeds the task median while coverage is slack; far-heavy helps iff the tolerance-scaled coverage cell is binding. Post-hoc on the three retrodicted tasks -- evidential weight rests on the pre-registered P-B2 calls. Factors: strategy consistency, funnel capacity, success-filter projector."},
  {"observation": "S4: within-pool per-attempt distance-success relation is noisy/sometimes positive while the region-level distance law is clean", "explanation_via": "Projection artifact, dissolved by construction: equal d_pos aliases wildly different channel loadings (receiver-heavy vs bridge-heavy vs rotation-heavy), so the scalar law is a lossy projection of a clean vector law -- the program's own red-team caveat becomes a derived prediction (P-C1 tests it). Factors: translation-invariance lemma, channel load vector."}
]

novelty_statement: Not the diversity/quality axes themselves -- Belkhale et al. (NeurIPS 2023) own that skeleton, DemInf packages it as I(S;A), MimicLabs splits diversity sub-types, and MimicGen's own appendices contain several explananda (Sec 6.3 skew, App H interpolation toxicity, App N noise trade, App R coverage bias, App S spread-vs-quality). What is new is (1) the meta-move: MimicGen's planned trajectory is a deterministic closed-form function of (source, transform draw, placement), so the entire planned pool is computable before one simulator step -- every prior use of such quantities (MimicGen App N.3 nearest-neighbor distance, MinInter's delta) is a selector inside generation, never an ex-ante audit instrument with generation and training logs demoted to held-out validation targets; (2) the physical localization and composition claim: quality lives in the source demo's slack profile and consistency structure, diversity lives in the transform sampler's spread over a TYPED per-object channel space, and the two compose additively in log-odds (measured, not assumed) -- a structural claim no prior work makes; (3) two theorems about the generator's own code path (translation-invariance with exactly four failure leaks; the 5-step/0.05 m transit ceiling) from which the channels, the receiving-object asymmetry, and the rotation surcharge fall out as corollaries -- prior art literally lacks the per-object vocabulary to state the flagship asymmetry claim; (4) three ours-only empirical anchors: per-object displacement asymmetry with failure-stage localization, extinction predicted from placement-free demo-intrinsic kinematic style (a different object from N.3/MinInter pairwise distance, which Table N.2 proves cannot be the quality axis), and intervention nulls/signs predicted by binding-cell logic; and (5) marginal-survivor mass μ -- the first non-circular per-source policy-toxicity predictor, scoring sources before generation and targeting policy value rather than survival, where existing curation either requires training (Re-Mix, CUPID) or scores already-executed data (DemInf). SkillGen showed motion planning helps; this framework says why, how much, and per task, ex ante. Claim discipline: six published facts (DGR-policy decoupling, interpolation toxicity, coverage-bias existence, noise trade-off, spread-vs-quality, inverted-U diversity) are cited as explananda and prior anchors, so the claimed contribution is purely the predictive ledger and the ours-only findings.
validation_plan:
[
  {"step": "Same-direction vs opposite-direction junction test: compute L_j from source segment endpoints + per-object displacements (pure pose arithmetic) for every attempt in e2_arms/<task>_N2/attempts.jsonl (dyaw=0 isolates the bridge channel); logistic regression of success on L_j vs d_pos at matched scene distance.", "cost": "Hours; zero new rollouts, zero training; existing logs as held-out targets only.", "falsifies_if": "L_j does not dominate d_pos, or same-direction displacement pairs show no survival advantage over opposite-direction pairs at matched d_pos -- kills the bridge channel and the threshold-shaped decline mechanism."},
  {"step": "P-A1 extinction/rank pre-registration: freeze the headroom/style composite and B_{i,s} extraction now (signs, windows, contact-event detector validated on source subtask_term_signals only), compute for all 10 sources x 9 tasks from hdf5 + meshes, publish predictions, then open per-source DGR -- validating on the never-used rotation-bearing e1 pools to purge the selection-on-outcome risk in the original screen.", "cost": "Days of pure computation; no generation, no training.", "falsifies_if": "Per-task Spearman < 0.5, or extinct sources (mug s7, square s2) fall outside the bottom decile of pre-computed budget, or the coffee-style sign-flip generalizes -- the demo-quality axis as specified is wrong."},
  {"step": "P-C1 frozen-transfer channel law: assemble the full load vector (m1, m2, symmetry-weighted lever rotation, L_j, absolute geography, clearance) with scales from geometry; fit ONE link + noise floor on stack's attempts, freeze, predict per-attempt success on the eight held-out tasks; publish the count of fitted scalars (ε, F, α, k) and sensitivity to frozen choices.", "cost": "About a week of engineering; existing logs only.", "falsifies_if": "AUC gain over scalar d_pos < 0.10 on held-out tasks, or the receiving channel is not the top separator within d_pos quintiles, or per-task refitting is needed -- the vector law degenerates to a relabeled per-task regression."},
  {"step": "P-C2 bridge intervention (the framework's unique mechanical prediction): predict ex ante, in pp per task per distance bin, the DGR recovered by scaling num_interpolation_steps proportionally to junction gap; change one config line, regenerate, compare.", "cost": "One config change + regeneration compute (no training); the cheapest decisive experiment in the program.", "falsifies_if": "Far-bin DGR does not recover by approximately the model-attributed bridge share, or near-bin DGR changes -- the bridge-lag mechanism is mis-scaled or confounded with collision."},
  {"step": "P-B1/P-B2 pre-registered policy-side calls: publish the G-index ancestry-harm ranking and density-direction signs (from source demos + C_s alone, with the Frechet/k-NN protocol pre-registered) for the hammer/mug ancestry arms and stack_three/hammer EXP-A arms BEFORE running them; then run.", "cost": "Computation is days; the confirming runs use the existing E2 training recipe (~6 seeds/arm at the established 5.8 runs/hour throughput).", "falsifies_if": "Out-of-sample harm ranking or direction signs miss -- the binding-cell layer loses its unique coverage (the nulls and signs) and reverts to post-hoc storytelling."},
  {"step": "P-A2 marginal-survivor toxicity: on a task unused for any calibration, construct two DGR-matched source pairs differing in pre-computed μ; generate matched-distance pools and train.", "cost": "The only step requiring new training (~2 pools x 6 seeds); run last, after steps 1-5 de-risk the survival law μ depends on.", "falsifies_if": "High-μ pair does not lose >= 5pp policy SR at matched distance and matched DGR -- μ fails to earn non-circular status and the quality axis collapses back to H(A|S) alone."}
]
improvement_levers:
[
  {"lever": "Gap-proportional interpolation steps (num_interpolation_steps ∝ predicted junction gap, optionally with num_fixed_steps dwell for catch-up)", "targets_factor": "Fixed-step target-anchored interpolation bridge", "expected_effect": "Recovers the bridge-attributed share of far-bin DGR loss at zero quality cost in near bins; simultaneously caps non-demonstrated-motion share growth. Predicted per task in pp by P-C2 before running."},
  {"lever": "Channel-aware source selection: pick the source minimizing the full load-to-budget ratio (per-object channels / that source's budget) instead of nearest scalar pose distance", "targets_factor": "Per-object channel load vector + contact-funnel residual budget", "expected_effect": "Strictly generalizes MimicGen N.3 and MinInter; largest gains where scalar distance aliases channel loadings (rotation-bearing and receiver-displaced attempts). Raises DGR without touching policy-side composition (Table N.2 pattern)."},
  {"lever": "Pre-generation source curation: drop or down-weight sources in the bottom decile of the frozen headroom/budget composite; prune strategy-outlier clusters flagged by the G-index instead of ancestry-balancing them", "targets_factor": "Lag-absorption headroom + strategy multiplicity/consistency", "expected_effect": "Eliminates wasted attempts on doomed sources (extinction set predicted ex ante) and prevents the stack-type ancestry harm (-7.5pp) by never reinjecting incompatible supervision."},
  {"lever": "Survivor-coverage-targeted attempt allocation: oversample placements where the frozen survival law predicts thinning (receiving-object far axis, workspace corners) so the POST-filter distribution, not the attempt distribution, matches the evaluation region", "targets_factor": "Success-only filter as coverage projector + funnel capacity C_s", "expected_effect": "Closes the App-R-style coverage holes behind corner cliffs (machine-only-far -24.1pp) at fixed total attempt compute; effect concentrated in tight-C_s tasks (coffee, threading), predicted null for stack."},
  {"lever": "Re-snapshot the receiving object's pose at placement-segment start (one extra pose query per subtask, or event-triggered on predicted high staleness exposure)", "targets_factor": "Single-snapshot pose staleness", "expected_effect": "Removes the receiver-nudge failure phenotype; gain proportional to receiver mobility and predicted lag Λ -- largest on free-standing receivers (coffee machine, nut), negligible on fixtures (drawers)."},
  {"lever": "Margin-aware filtering: keep the success filter but drop survivors with predicted residual margin below k·ε (reduce μ), and retain σ noise rather than trading it away for DGR", "targets_factor": "Marginal-survivor mass μ + action noise as robustness probe", "expected_effect": "Converts the DGR-vs-policy trade explicitly: modest DGR cost for removal of razor-margin training examples; predicted policy gain wherever P-A2 shows a μ-ordered gap, and a principled replacement for the current practice of zeroing noise when generation collapses."}
]
